1tkKurUEJj0ROUhCQs6Q9r.title: Someday We'll Linger in the Sun

s.t: Gaelynn Lea says it came to her in the shower: she had the first line, which festered in her brain for about a month before she finally wrote it.
s.src: MPR News: Meet Duluth's Gaelynn Lea, the 2016 Tiny Desk Contest winner
s.q: Well, this particular song came to me when I was in the shower. ... I had the first line, and it kind of festered in my brain for about a month, and then finally I wrote it.

s.t: Gaelynn Lea wrote it while her wedding plans were in limbo: a song about love, ‘but not flowery love, more marital love and the challenges that come with it’.
s.src: The Herald (Everett): Tiny Desk champion Gaelynn Lea enjoying her moment in the sun
s.q: The inspiration for “Someday We’ll Linger in the Sun” came when their wedding plans were put in limbo. ... “It’s a song about love — but not flowery love, more marital love and the challenges that come with it.”

s.t: For Learning How to Stay, Gaelynn Lea re-recorded the song that won her NPR’s Tiny Desk Contest with ‘more of a rock vibe’ and a slightly more intense, aggressive energy.
s.src: No Depression: Gaelynn Lea Focuses on Appreciating the Moment on ‘Learning How to Stay’
s.q: For example, I re-recorded “Someday We’ll Linger in the Sun” to be more of a rock vibe, with a slightly more intense or aggressive energy. ... But I think the meaning still holds true either way it’s played.

s.t: Gaelynn Lea’s memoir was first to be called Linger in the Sun, after it, but became It Wasn’t Meant to Be Perfect, as the old title didn’t fit the story.
s.q: It was going to originally be called Linger in the Sun, but it didn't feel like it fit the arc of the story, even though that is the song that, Some Day We Will Linger in the Sun, the song is the song that I entered into the Tiny Desk

s.t: Gaelynn Lea’s earlier Tiny Desk Contest video of it, shot by her friend Leah Nelson, avoids showing her at first so her disability isn’t the first impression.
s.src: MPR News: Meet Duluth's Gaelynn Lea, the 2016 Tiny Desk Contest winner
s.q: my friend Leah [Nelson] and I shot the video together in my office ... And she actually thought of doing that angle ... Because when you have a disability, especially one like mine where it's pretty visible — I didn't want that to necessarily be the first impression.

f.t: Asked to write the music for Broadway’s Macbeth, she didn’t know who its star Daniel Craig was, until the director explained that he had been James Bond.
f.q: finally the director had to be like, well, Daniel Craig is playing Macbeth, but I didn't know who that was. I never know who any celebrities are. And so I was like, oh, has he been in movies or something? And he's like, he was James Bond.

f.t: Alan Sparhawk of the band Low gave her a looping pedal, telling her to learn it because someday she would do shows by herself.
f.src: Sound of Boston: Interview: Gaelynn Lea
f.q: Then he gave me a looping pedal and said, “You should learn how to use this, and someday you’ll do shows by yourself,”

f.t: Before she could even read, she was in her first play: her lines were recorded on a cassette tape and she learned them by ear.
f.src: MPR News: Meet Duluth's Gaelynn Lea, the 2016 Tiny Desk Contest winner
f.q: Before I could even read, I was in my first play. They had to record my lines on a cassette tape and I learned them by hearing them.

f.t: In New York for an NPR concert, she played waltzes to subway passengers late one night; busking, she said, is ‘one of the purest ways a musician can connect’.
f.src: The Herald (Everett): Tiny Desk champion Gaelynn Lea enjoying her moment in the sun
f.q: recounting her trip to New York a few weeks earlier for a National Public Radio concert. She wound up performing waltzes on the subway for passengers late one night. “It’s one of the purest ways a musician can connect with people.”

f.t: Before her Tiny Desk win she taught fiddle lessons and her husband, Paul, was a university custodian; the flood of invitations that followed put them both on the road.
f.q: He was a custodian at UMD and I taught fiddle lessons ... And then when I won the Tiny Desk, the thing I wasn't expecting ... people from all over the country were like, could you come play at our venue?
